svg.text: Phase 5 · milestone 7 · Calculated fields and derived meters: layout options
Dark theme. Formulas use stable keys, + − × ÷, parentheses, and functions (mean, median, geometric_mean, harmonic_mean, min, max, sum, count, round, abs, stddev).
Units are checked by dimension. Worked out when shown, never stored. The ƒ badge marks a worked-out value.
Setup → Custom fields → + Calculated field. Type freely, or insert from the two menus. Here: cost per mile, and average trip time.
1 · Typed formula, with Functions ▾ and Values ▾ menus
Checked as you type; a preview from the latest event. Both menus insert at the cursor.
Over (for a function over past events):
Last X events, days, weeks, months, or mi / km (or h on an hour meter).
On the latest fuel-up (12 Nov): $0.14 per mi
Refused, with the reason: "trip-time + volume: can't add a time to a volume."
Each by its stable key, labels beside.
A fuel-up with Cost per mile and Average trip time (last 5).
2A · On the form (live) and the event page
Read-only rows under the fields, marked ƒ
Changes as Cost and the odometer are typed.
The form stays as it is
Setup → Meters. Here: equivalent miles = odometer + idle hours × 33. Nobody types its readings.
3A · "Worked out from other meters" in + Meter
One dialog; the choice swaps readings for a formula
✓ Distance + Time × distance per time = Distance
Interval rules can use it; it can't be reset.
Its dialog: 3A's name, unit, and formula, without the choice
4 · A derived meter on the vehicle
One layout: in the Overview's meters and Setup, marked ƒ; never a reading field on a form.
worked out from Odometer and Idle hours
One layout: "ⓘ How to write one" beside every formula box opens a short popup; "Full guide" opens the Help page.
5A · A short popup, then the full guide
Values by their key; numbers with a unit (33 mi/h).
+ − × ÷ and ( ). Units must agree: miles + hours is refused.
A function over past events takes an Over: last 5, last 3 months,
· Every function, with an example each
· Every Over, and how history is chosen
· Units: which combine, and what they make
· Derived meters, and rules that use them
· Why a formula is refused, and the fix
In the app, so it works offline too.
Chosen: 1 (combined), 2A, 3B, 4A; the ƒ badge everywhere a value is worked out; 5A help beside every formula box.
